bib.title: Agent Data Protocol: Unifying Datasets for Diverse, Effective Fine-tuning of LLM Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Agent Data Protocol: Unifying Datasets for Diverse, Effective Fine-Tuning of LLM Agents", Yueqi Song (first author) ... Graham Neubig (CMU, OSU, HKU, Duke, Fujitsu, All Hands AI). Header: "Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026". arXiv:2510.24702v2, 4 Mar 2026 (v1 Oct 2025). Project: agentdataprotocol.com.

COVERAGE: 21 of 21 pages, 69,263 chars, all read, including the appendices (A-F). I read the references only for origins. No extraction faults.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. ADP is a Pydantic schema, a hub-and-spoke "interlingua" between raw agent datasets and agent-specific SFT formats. The trajectory content is an alternating list of Actions (API, Code, Message) and Observations (Text, Web).
 number: 13 datasets unified, 1.3M trajectories ("ADP Dataset V1"), 3 target harnesses (OpenHands, SWE-Agent, AgentLab)
 setup: the datasets cover coding, SWE, tool use and web.
 quote: "we implement converters from 13 preexisting datasets into ADP, and converters from ADP to 3 different agent architectures... consisting of 1.3M training trajectories, dubbed the ADP Dataset V1."
 where: p.2
2. SFT on mixed ADP data beats the untuned base model on every benchmark and scale.
 number: SWE-Bench Verified, Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct, SWE-Agent: 7B 0.4% to 20.2%, 14B 2.0% to 34.4%, 32B 2.2% to 40.3%. OpenHands: 7B 2.8% to 20.4%, 14B 5.8% to 30.6%, 32B 10.6% to 36.8%.
 setup: LLaMA-Factory SFT. Single reported numbers; no seeds or variance are reported.
 quote: "Qwen-2.5-7B-Coder-Instruct improves from 0.4% to 20.2% (+19.8%) with SWE-Agent and from 2.8% to 20.4% (+17.6%) with OpenHands."
 where: p.7-8, Tables 3-5
 Other results (AgentLab for WebArena; OpenHands for AgentBench OS and GAIA):
 - WebArena: 7B 4.5% to 21.0%, 14B 5.5% to 22.2%, 32B 10.9% to 22.9%
 - AgentBench OS: 7B 3.5% to 27.1%, 14B 2.8% to 20.8%, 32B 27.8% to 34.7%
 - GAIA: 7B 7.3% to 9.1% (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct)
 The headline "~20% average gain" is stated in the abstract and not computed anywhere.
3. ADP data matches or beats single-dataset SOTA baselines.
 number: 32B SWE-Agent: ADP 40.3% vs SWE-smith 40.2%. 32B OpenHands: ADP 36.8% vs SWE-Gym 20.6%. 7B SWE-Agent: ADP 20.2% vs SWE-smith 15.2%. 7B OpenHands: ADP 20.4% vs SWE-Gym 10.6%.
 setup: the baseline rows are "collected from previous works", not retrained. The paper also compares against Claude 3.5 Sonnet with SWE-Agent (33.6%) and Claude 3 Opus (15.8%).
 quote: "matching or exceeding Claude 3.5 Sonnet with SWE-Agent's 33.6% performance"
 where: p.8-9
4. The mix transfers across tasks better than single-dataset training, which can cause negative transfer.
 number, with the single-dataset baseline first and ADP second: SWE-Bench, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: SWE-smith only 1.0% vs ADP 10.4%. SWE-Bench, Qwen3-8B: CodeActInstruct+Code-Feedback 0.2%, SWE-smith only 11.0%, ADP 16.6%. WebArena: Go-Browse only 16.0% vs ADP 20.1%. AgentBench OS, Qwen3-8B: AgentInstruct only 21.5% vs ADP 25.7%. GAIA: AgentInstruct only 0.6% vs ADP 9.1%.
 setup: Table 6, OpenHands or AgentLab harness, 7-8B models.
 quote: "ADP consistently outperforms task-specific tuning on the target task and, critically, avoids the negative transfer that single-domain tuning often induces on other tasks"
 where: p.9, Table 6
5. The gain is not just data volume.
 number: Qwen3-8B on SWE-Bench with OpenHands, about 30K samples each: SWE-smith up-sampled 11.0% vs ADP 16.6%.
 quote: "SWE-smith training yields 11.0% accuracy, whereas ADP training achieves 16.6% under a comparable number of samples."
 where: p.20, App. E.1, Table 10
 Caveat: this is the only matched-size control. It covers SWE-Bench only, and the baseline is up-sampled repetition.
6. Engineering cost is linear rather than quadratic.
 number: 4,892 LOC to convert the 13 datasets to ADP (AgentInstruct about 1500, openhands-feedback 879, Mind2Web 476, Code-Feedback 134). The ADP-to-SFT converter takes about 77 LOC on average (OpenHands about 150, SWE-Agent about 50, AgentLab about 30). For A=100 harnesses, 489,200 LOC without ADP vs 12,592 with ADP.
 setup: the 100-harness figure is extrapolated, with LOC as the proxy for effort.
 quote: "CostADP(A, D) ≈ 4892 + 77×100 = 12,592 for A = 100"
 where: p.10
7. Cross-dataset statistics from Table 2 (p.6).
 number: average 10.1 rounds per trajectory, from 1.0 (Synatra) to 26.8 (SWE-smith). Overall action mix is 53% API, 24% code, 23% message. Function-thought coverage is 83.8% overall, with Mind2Web at 0.0% and SWE-Gym at 42.0%.
8. Mixture details (Appendix C, p.18-19).
 - Per-dataset multipliers w_d: orca agentinstruct 0.001, synatra 0.01, code-feedback 0.1, nebius 0.2, swe-gym 3 (up), agenttuning subsets 2 (up), the rest 1.
 - Domain filtering: OpenHands and SWE-Agent train on the non-web data only (about 30K samples). AgentLab trains on the web data only (about 20K samples).
 - Sampling uses a fixed random seed and shuffles each epoch.
 - The multipliers are hand-set. There was no mixture search.

LIMITS
- There is no ablation of mixing weights or of the contribution of individual datasets. The authors say: "Future experiments could explore different sampling multipliers and examine the effect of each dataset on coding and software engineering tasks."
- Each harness is trained on a domain-filtered subset (non-web or web). Only about 30K or 20K of the 1.3M trajectories are actually used, so the "1.3M" headline is not the training size.
- Table 3-5 baselines are copied from prior papers, so the harnesses, prompts and base models may differ. Some baselines use other bases (Llama-2-chat for AgentBench, Llama-3.1-8B for NNetNav).
- No seeds, runs or confidence intervals are reported. The extraction shows single numbers throughout.
- The matched-scale control is SWE-only. The Table 6 baselines vary in size and quality.
- GAIA gains are small at 7B (+1.8 points). There is no 14B or 32B GAIA result.
- Text only. Multimodality is listed as future work. The paper also lists standardized evaluation and environments, and community growth and quality validation, as future directions.
- Quality assurance is automated format checks only, such as an 80% threshold for thought-paired tool calls. The paper does no data-quality filtering or deduplication study.
- The paper does no RL. This is SFT only.
- Authors' interpretive claim: "Overall, mixed ADP tuning yields stronger in-domain accuracy and cross-task generalization than single-domain tuning." The paper does not isolate causes beyond the equal-scale test.

BUILDS ON
Existing datasets: AgentInstruct (Zeng et al., 2023), CodeActInstruct (Wang et al., 2024b), Code-Feedback (Zheng et al., 2024a), Mind2Web (Deng et al., 2023), SWE-Gym (Pan et al., 2025), SWE-smith (Yang et al., 2025b), Synatra (Ou et al., 2024), NNetNav (Murty et al., 2024), Go-Browse (Gandhi & Neubig, 2025), Orca AgentInstruct (Mitra et al., 2024), Nebius SWE trajectories (Golubev et al., 2024). Harnesses: OpenHands (Wang et al., 2025), SWE-Agent (Yang et al., 2024), AgentLab/BrowserGym (Drouin et al., 2024; de Chezelles et al., 2025). Training: LLaMA-Factory (Zheng et al., 2024b). Related standardization work cited: Agent-FLAN (Chen et al., 2024, Findings of ACL 2024), AgentBank (Song et al., 2024), Zhang et al. 2024/2025 and Xi et al. 2025. These are named as "task-specific or agent-specific unification". Negative-transfer citations: Mueller et al. 2024, Kotha et al. 2024, Li et al. 2024.

CODE
The ADP trajectory format is the Pydantic schema in App. B.2 (p.16-17). Entries have class_ values text_observation, code_action and message_action. Fields are id, content[], and details. Per-class fields: code_action has language, content and description (the thought). text_observation has content, name and source (user or environment).

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.2): the ADP overview with action and observation types and example conversions.
- Fig 2 (p.6): the O(D x A) vs O(D + A) hub-and-spoke comparison.
- Fig 3 and 4 (p.19): scaling of base vs ADP-trained models at 7B, 14B and 32B, and the gains.

PROBLEMS
Table text is flattened in the extraction, but the numbers read cleanly and agree with the prose. The arXiv v2 date comes from the page-1 stamp. No embedded instructions found.

KEY VERBATIM QUOTES FOR THE NOTE
(1) p.1 abstract: "we unified a broad collection of 13 existing agent training datasets into ADP format... demonstrated an average performance gain of ∼20% over corresponding base models".
(2) p.2: "the issue is not a lack of data, but rather a lack of standardization."
(3) p.9: "ADP consistently outperforms task-specific tuning on the target task and, critically, avoids the negative transfer that single-domain tuning often induces on other tasks".
